key_insight: An adult-trained kidney MRI segmentation model showed promising transfer to pediatric Wilms tumors, but non-inferiority to a pediatric-specific model was not demonstrated.
clinical_relevance: Adult MRI datasets may help develop pediatric tumor segmentation tools, although these findings concern imaging rather than cancer drug discovery.
method: Trained a segmentation model on single-sequence T1- or T2-weighted adult kidney MRI.
Evaluated it on held-out adult scans and pediatric Wilms tumor scans.
Compared pediatric performance with a pediatric-specific nnU-Net using Dice scores and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance.
evidence_signal: Median lesion Dice scores were 0.86 on adult test scans and 0.85 on pediatric scans, versus 0.90 for the pediatric-specific model.
watch_item: Non-inferiority was not established, underscoring the value of pediatric training data and further validation before clinical use.
paper_title: From Adult Renal Masses to Pediatric Wilms Tumors: Evaluating Cross-Domain Generalization of Kidney Lesion Segmentation on MRI
